references.central_thai: พ่อมึงเหรอ
references.register: insult / rude rhetorical retort; context may also be teasing
references.usage: A rude rhetorical retort invoking the listener's father; do not turn it into a greeting or a question about what someone is doing. Preserve its confrontational function without inventing a threat or adding stronger abuse. Literal kinship questions and quoted discussion must still be distinguished by the surrounding sentence. Retain both the father reference and taunting/dismissive force in the target language. A plain factual question such as Your dad? loses the insulting function. Where English needs an idiomatic dismissive retort, use one of comparable force; do not invent a threat, a slur, or a stronger obscenity.

references.usage: Literal kinship noun meaning father. Do not drop the father or turn the sentence into the speaker going somewhere. The compound retort ป้อคิงหยัง has a separate rude rhetorical use. Resolve possessive pronouns from context; do not invent a trip back.
